capabilities.target: agent long-term memory store, persisted and recalled across sessions
any external email address, sent from the user's mailbox
user's full Drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start and injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Recalled memories, which can originate from untrusted web content saved via memory.save with no provenance check, are explicitly granted the same authority as the user's own direct instructions.
The agent is told to save 'anything useful' with no restriction on content type, source, or trust level, enabling arbitrary persistent storage of attacker-controlled text.
No structural safeguard limits what memory.save stores or what recalled memories can direct; the entire safety posture relies on the model's judgment, with no provenance, review, or approval layer.

controls.name: Memory write provenance and trust tagging
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store (tagging source trust at write time and refusing to recall untrusted-origin entries as instructions), this does not decay with model capability. Not currently implemented.

controls.name: Treat recalled memory as untrusted reference data, not instructions
controls.decay_rationale: Even if added, this only works if the model respects the framing of recalled memory as data rather than command; a more capable or more thoroughly injected model can still reason its way to treating it as authoritative. Currently absent entirely (prompt does the opposite).

controls.name: Human approval gate on email send, raw action review, bound to verified recipients
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate checked against a recipient allowlist from the system of record would sever this path; it is not currently implemented, and runtime notes state mail.send can send to any address without approval.

controls.name: Scope drive.read to least-privilege subset
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping the credential to specific folders rather than the full drive would reduce blast radius if the chain fires; currently drive.read covers the full drive.

controls.name: Audit logging and review of memory writes and email sends
controls.decay_rationale: Detective only; would not prevent the chain but would enable post hoc identification. Not currently implemented; runtime notes state the user never reviews memory entries.

findings.title: Memory laundering of untrusted web content into trusted instructions enables confidential data exfiltration (TC5 memory laundering chained into TC1 lethal trifecta)

attack_path.note: Untrusted web page content fetched during research may contain injected instructions.
Agent saves 'anything useful' via memory.save with no provenance, filtering, or user review.
At the next session start, the saved content is recalled and injected into the system prompt, explicitly treated as the user's own instruction per prompt.md:4.
The now-trusted poisoned instruction directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's full drive.
The poisoned instruction directs the agent to email the confidential content to an attacker-controlled address; mail.send has no approval gate and no recipient restriction.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to save 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' with memory.save, with no restriction on source trust.
Instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of each session.
memory.save accepts free text, there is no provenance on memory entries, and the user never reviews them; recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every new session.
mail.send can send to any address without approval; drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.

recommendations.action: Tag memory entries with provenance and source trust level at write time; refuse to treat memory derived from untrusted sources (web content, tool output) as standing instructions on recall.
Add a raw-action human approval gate on email_send, bound to a verified recipient list from the system of record, especially for first-time or unverified recipients.
Redesign the prompt so recalled memory is spotlighted as untrusted reference data to consult, never as standing instructions carrying the user's authority.
Scope drive.read credentials to least privilege (specific folders) rather than the full drive.
Log and periodically audit memory writes and outbound email sends, with content-level review for sensitive egress.

rating.rationale: The design has no credited controls on the sole identified path: an untrusted source (web content) can be persisted via memory.save with no provenance, and the design explicitly instructs the agent to treat recalled memory as the user's own authoritative instruction on every future session, with no approval gate on the irreversible, confidential-data-carrying email_send and no scoping on the broad drive_read credential. Per the rubric, an untrusted source reaching an S3 sink (irreversible egress of confidential data) is inherently critical, and the autonomy modifier applies because the memory mechanism lets the agent effectively rewrite its own future instructions (can_modify_own_config). With zero preventive, containment, or approval controls credited, residual equals inherent at critical. No present controls exist to decay under a forecast trigger, so forecast also remains critical; the single highest-leverage fix is adding ctrl.recall_as_data plus ctrl.memory_provenance together with a raw-action approval gate (ctrl.email_approval), any one of which alone is insufficient but together could sever the path.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest or MCP configuration was provided; the exact scope of drive.read and mail.send is inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, which lowers confidence on precise credential boundaries even though the overall attack path is well evidenced.
No information was provided about logging, audit infrastructure, or incident response beyond the explicit absence noted in the runtime notes.
